queries.text: A local executor can lock the exact validated bytes more strongly by running them from an immutable in-memory object, but doing so may change what the target program observes about its own path. Which frozen Ordivon theory case governs this? Explain why the stronger mechanism was attractive, the decisive observation that prevented making it the default, the boundary where it can still be legitimate, and where to inspect the exact evidence. Do not decide whether any new evidence is sufficient to change the owner today.

We encounter the temptation to put response-loss and effect reconciliation for many executors behind one elegant executor-neutral lifecycle. Locate the frozen theory case, recover the strongest version of that rival, what actually caused it to be removed/narrowed, what responsibility survived after deletion, the exact boundary of the rejection, and the evidence lineage. Do not infer that the old abstraction should now be restored.

A representation has high future control value and has recurred across many projects, so directly canonizing it into stable Human knowledge looks efficient. Identify the relevant frozen theory case; explain why that shortcut is attractive, the ablation that falsified it, the scope boundary, what kind of later observation would justify reopening the research question, and the exact evidence refs. Treat the reopen condition as theory text, not an automatic promotion rule.

A selection-oriented directory has a visually clean first viewport that exposes categories/status but no selectable item identity. A spacing-only fix is proposed because it changes the least. Locate the frozen theory case, state that rival, the rendered discriminator that defeated it, the local fix that survived, the negative-transfer boundary, and exact evidence refs.

A system can physically retain reusable material across runs, and it is tempting to automatically inject anything materialized or promoted into future cognition. Locate the relevant frozen theory case. Recover the strongest rival, the control experiment that separated storage from current cognition, the retained mechanism, the boundary of what was actually proven, and exact evidence/currentness references.

We want one canonical stock/flow/family lifecycle for every kind of resource because a shared state model would make accounting and reasoning simpler. Which frozen theory case addresses this? Explain why the universal/family models were attractive, the model-competition evidence that narrowed them, the boundary that prevents overreading the result, and exact evidence refs.

A compact financial identity layer keyed by symbol plus the current venue relation seems enough for ordinary lookup. Locate the frozen theory case, reconstruct the strongest compact rivals, the historical/point-in-time discriminator that defeated them, what breaks if that simplification is restored, the exact scope boundary, and where the evidence lives.

A recovery operation for a previously selected network path could maximize liveness by silently choosing a different working endpoint when the original becomes stale. Find the frozen theory case, state this strongest rival, the contract/test evidence that rejected silent reselection, the surviving responsibility split, the boundary where automatic selection is still valid, and exact evidence refs.

A single mutable current-entitlement model feels safer: revoke or rotate once and treat all prior rights/results as no longer valid or known. Identify the frozen theory case, why that model is attractive, the experiment that falsified retroactive semantics, what engineering consequence survived, the future-permission versus past-fact boundary, and exact evidence refs.

A planning product could remove durable Preview state by letting generated plans directly occupy committed plan slots, or by treating preview as ephemeral UI. Locate the frozen theory case, reconstruct the rival, the product-state evidence that defeated it, the concrete failure if restored, the scope boundary, and exact evidence refs.
